problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)={x}^{2}(t)+{y}^{2}(t)-3x(t)-y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=2x(t)-{y}^{2}(t)+5y(t)-8\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of ODEs above. An equilibrium point of the system is $[1,\,2]^{T}.$ Which of the following is the system obtained by shifting this equilibrium to the origin?

feedback.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)={x}^{2}(t)+3x(t)+y(t)+1 \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-3x(t)-{y}^{2}(t)+2y(t)-4\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of ODEs above. An equilibrium point of the system is $[-1,\,1]^{T}.$ Which of the following is the system obtained by shifting this equilibrium to the origin?
feedback.worked_solution:
To shift the system's equilibrium from ${x}^{∗}$ to the origin, we define the deviation vector

$$
u=x-{x}^{∗},
$$

where $x=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]$ and $u=[\begin{aligned}u(t) \\ v(t)\end{aligned}].$

In our case, we have

$$
u=x-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,⇒\,x=u+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,\text{and}\,{x}^{′}={u}^{′}.
$$

In coordinate form, this can be written as follows:

$$
x(t)=u(t)-1,\,y(t)=v(t)+1,\,{x}^{′}(t)={u}^{′}(t),\,{v}^{′}(t)={y}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now substitute these into the given system.

- Substituting into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & ={x}^{2}(t)+3x(t)+y(t)+1 \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =(u(t)-1)^{2}+3(u(t)-1)+(v(t)+1)+1 \\  & =({u}^{2}(t)-2u(t)+1)+3u(t)-3+v(t)+1+1 \\  & ={u}^{2}(t)+u(t)+v(t).\end{aligned}
$$

- Substituting into the second equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =-3x(t)-{y}^{2}(t)+2y(t)-4 \\ {v}^{′}(t) & =-3(u(t)-1)-(v(t)+1)^{2}+2(v(t)+1)-4 \\  & =-3u(t)+3-({v}^{2}(t)+2v(t)+1)+2v(t)+2-4 \\  & =-3u(t)-{v}^{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the shifted system is the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{u}^{′}(t)={u}^{2}(t)+u(t)+v(t) \\ {v}^{′}(t)=-3u(t)-{v}^{2}(t)\end{aligned}
$$
